prompt: A ladder leans against a wall at a $65^\circ$ angle with the ground and touches the wall $12$ ft above the ground. How long is the ladder, in feet, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: This time the unknown is the hypotenuse and the known side is opposite the $65^\circ$ angle.

hints.text: This time the unknown is the hypotenuse and the known side is opposite the $65^\circ$ angle.
$\sin 65^\circ = \frac{12}{L}$ — the unknown is downstairs, so multiply both sides by $L$ first.

explanation: The height $12$ ft is opposite the $65^\circ$ angle and the ladder $L$ is the hypotenuse, so use sine.
Write $\sin 65^\circ = \frac{12}{L}$; because $L$ is in the denominator, solve by $L = \frac{12}{\sin 65^\circ}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The hypotenuse is always biggest
steps: Whatever you compute, the ladder must be longer than the $12$ ft it reaches up the wall.
$13.2 > 12$ ✓. If you had multiplied instead of divided you would have gotten $10.9$ ft — shorter than the wall height, which is impossible.
